newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ministry to revise targets for 1997. The Commerce Ministry is to revise the country's import and export targets for 1997 to ensure the current account deficit next year does not exceed 7.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), said Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasenee.

Although Dr Narongchai initiated a 15 percent growth policy, the president of the Thailand Development and Research Institute, Dr Chalongphob Sussangkarn, also called for the trade deficit target to be set in line with macroeconomic policy. (BANGKOK POST)

- "Young-Turk senators" short-list CDA hopefuls. A group of 31 first-time senators have short-listed candidates for the people's representative seats on the Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) from 50 provinces having previously vetted the specialist nominees.
Senator Wallop Tangkhananulak said yesterday the group will pass details of its favoured nominees to other senators and that he expects at least 50 senators to receive the information.

The group, dubbed the "young-Turk senators," is racing against time to complete its self-appointed task. There are 760 candidates for the 76 people's representative seats on the CDA. A joint sitting of parliamanent will on Thursday select the 76 people's members and the 23 specialist members. (THE NATION)
- Call to watch all borrowing. Borrowing by state-run organisations from both local and foreign sources should be monitored, according to a prominent economist.

Chalongphob Sussangkarn, president of the Thailand Development and Reserach Institute, said the government currently monitored only state enterprise spending using foreign capital and failed to watch loans from local banks and finance houses. (BUSINESS POST)

- Instability a major offput for investors. Why have investors continued to throw away Thai stocks, disregarding economic fundamentals?. The answer is simple - they do not think the government, or the action plan recently unveiled by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan in particular, is addressing the real problem, which is growing instability of the Thai economiy.

Stability must be the key policy objective of the Chavalit administration if it really hopes to cure the present economic ills. Yet what investors have found in Amnuay's action plan is largely a stimulatory package ranging from a loosened monetary policy and export boost to commercial property bailout. (NATION BUSINESS)
